newsitem.title: DENMARK: Maersk Air cabin staff call March strike.
newsitem.headline: Maersk Air cabin staff call March strike.

text.p: Danish airline Maersk Air cabin staff called a strike for March 1 in support of claims for more pay and better working conditions, Danish news agency Ritzau reported on Wednesday.

"We have worked to make Maersk Air competitive and now we want to be properly paid for our efforts. We do not want to be worse off than cabin staff in other airlines," a Maersk Air cabin attendants' spokesman said.
Maersk's 260 cabin attendants have failed in protracted talks to reach agreement with management on a new pay and working conditions accord.
Insistence by Maersk management on retiring all cabin staff at the age of 50 has particularly upset the attendants, the spokesman said.
Maersk cabin staff are not demanding any specific pay increase, but insisting on a closer dialogue with management on their conditions, he said.
Maersk Air, owned by Danish shipping and oil group A.P. Moeller, operates flights within Denmark and the Nordic region as well as between Copenhagen and London and charter flights.

If no new talks take place, the dispute is expected to be sent to the government arbitration panel, which has the power to postpone strike action and ultimately to impose a settlement. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
